h: The Floozie, the Hoard and a few frames
p: Locals have a nickname for the big reclining bronze figure in Victoria Square: the Floozie in the Jacuzzi. Officially it's called The River, and it's one of those landmarks every Brummie knows. Have a look on the way in, it's a classic part of any city-centre wander.

Just behind the square, Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery is home to part of the Staffordshire Hoard, a remarkable find of Anglo-Saxon gold and silver metalwork. Check it's open before you go, as the museum has had sections closed for refurbishment in recent years. Birmingham Town Hall, the grand building modelled on a Roman temple, hosts concerts and events if you want a cultured start to the evening.

Some practical tips for the bowling side. Bring photo ID if you look young, because bar venues commonly check. Book ahead if you've got a group, and think about two lanes rather than one for a big party, so nobody spends half the night waiting for a turn. Mixing in some of the other bar games is a nice way to keep everyone involved.

In the run-up to Christmas, Victoria Square and the streets around it have traditionally hosted Birmingham's popular German-style Christmas market, which brings big crowds. If you're visiting then, allow extra time to get through the city and book your lane well in advance.
